text: {"hypotheses":[{"statement":"Periodic consolidation (compression) of stored facts mitigates the accuracy drop observed when the memory exceeds ~40 items by reducing cross‑fact interference, which explains why the bounded‑memory variant remains accurate and why MemGPT’s paging‑style management improves performance.","confidence":0.78,"support_ids":["562412ff","333b655e","72ccf918","a962f389"],"tags":["consolidation","interference","accuracy_drop","bounded_memory"]},{"statement":"The naive‑append memory strategy’s token‑budget overflow is the underlying cause of the QA accuracy degradation seen after 40 items, so enforcing a fixed token budget (e.g., via windowed or bounded memory) is necessary to maintain stable performance.","confidence":0.65,"support_ids":["562412ff","9858241e","333b655e"],"tags":["token_budget","append_vs_rewrite","accuracy_drop","windowed_memory"]}]}
